title: Outcome-led initiative onboarding and quarterly sequencing
creator: Ava Moreno
description:
Goal: Design and implement a repeatable, lightweight flow that onboards company-level initiatives into the quarterly roadmap in an outcome-first way.

Problem statement: Current initiative intake often focuses on features and outputs rather than the customer outcome or metric to move. This causes inconsistent prioritization across teams, brittle cross-functional dependencies, and unclear gating for rollouts.

Scope:
- Define an "initiative charter" template (outcome, leading metric, primary hypothesis, success criteria, owner, critical dependencies).
- Create a quarterly sequencing rhythm: intake -> staging -> handshake -> commit -> live-checks.
- Align Linear workflow states and labels to the charter stages so PM/Eng/Design can operationalize handoffs.
- Build a lightweight automation (Zapier/partial script) to populate initiative metadata into Linear and the roadmap board.
- Pilot with three cross-functional initiatives from Q2 candidate list (Serving runtime efficiency, Console rollouts, Dedicated autoscaling policies).

Non-goals: full OKR tool integration or a heavy governance process. We can iterate toward stricter gating after the pilot.

Success metrics:
- 90% of company initiatives onboarded with complete charter fields before commit.
- 30% reduction in post-commit dependency escalations for pilot initiatives by end of Q2.
- Stakeholder satisfaction >= 4/5 in post-pilot survey.

Trade-offs and decisions to make:
- Lightweight vs prescriptive: prefer minimal friction; require only critical charter fields to avoid blocking innovation.
- Centralized sequencing team vs distributed owners: pilot with a small central facilitator team (PM Ops + Strategy) but keep ownership with initiative leads.
- Automation vs manual templates: build template + simple automation first; postpone heavy integrations to avoid scope creep.

Rollout plan:
1) Week 0-2: finalize charter template and Linear state/label conventions.
2) Week 2-4: create Confluence PRD, onboarding checklist, and run a 1-hour training for initiative owners.
3) Week 4-10: pilot with three initiatives; collect weekly sync notes and blockers.
4) Week 10-12: retro, iterate on charter, and propose adoption for Q3 planning.

Expected stakeholders: PMs owning initiatives, Eng leads (serving/runtime, infra), Design leads, Reliability & Observability, GTM reps.

Open questions:
- Which specific Linear state names cause least friction for engineers? (proposal: Staged, Handshake, Committed, Live-check)
- Scope of mandatory metrics: should we require both leading and lagging metrics? (recommendation: require one leading metric + one lagging success metric)
- How to surface blocked initiative dependencies in the Console dashboard (owner: Observability team to advise).
updates: 2026-02-16: Kickoff meeting with PM Ops, Strategy, Eng infra, and Design. Agreed to focus pilot on three initiatives: runtime batching improvements, console rollout for rollout policies, and Dedicated autoscaling UX.

2026-02-22: Drafted charter template in Confluence. Added fields for outcome statement, primary hypothesis, leading metric, lagging metric, acceptance criteria, and critical dependencies. Link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OKR/Initiative+Charter+Template

2026-03-01: Linear state proposal reviewed with Eng leads. Feedback: prefer 'Handshake' over 'Staged' to emphasize cross-team agreement. Action: update Linear workflow and add automation to tag owners on handshake transition.

2026-03-05: Design reviewed the onboarding checklist; suggested adding a simple 'API/Infra risk' quick-assessment to capture migration/compatibility needs. DES-2045 added to dependencies for creating a risk card template.

2026-03-09: Implemented a lightweight Zap that copies charter metadata to initiative Linear ticket when a new Confluence charter is published. Pilot automation PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/okrs/pull/78
2026-03-12: Pilot kickoff scheduled. Week 1 pilot sync cadence: twice-weekly 30-minute checkpoints. Preparing pre-pilot survey and dashboard filters to track blocked dependencies.
acceptance_criteria: Charter template published and accessible to all initiative owners (Confluence link in docs).
Linear workflow states and labels updated and documented in onboarding checklist.
Automation exists to seed Linear tickets from Confluence charters (can be manual-run by PM Ops).
Pilot executed on three initiatives with weekly sync notes and at least one dependency resolved via the handshake step.
Post-pilot retro and recommended next steps documented and presented to Exec PM forum.
